description: A towering walking machine has three articulated legs, a moving brazen hood, flexible metallic tentacles and rear carrier. It can bend knees, shorten legs and cross water.
game_adaptation: Central combat threat; stage a reachable foot or lowered joint so dash and slash remain meaningful.

title: Heat-Ray case and parabolic projection
description: An invisible heat beam ignites combustibles, softens metal, damages glass and flashes water to steam. The generator appears as a camera-like case; a parabolic-mirror mechanism is proposed rather than proven.
game_adaptation: Pale floor shapes and moving tells communicate aim; flame, steam and debris convey active heat.

title: Black Smoke canisters and launching tube
description: A thick black tube launches canisters that break on impact without explosive detonation, releasing heavy lethal vapour that pools low and settles to dust.
game_adaptation: A bounded ground-hazard pattern with generous clean landing pockets.

title: Steam jet apparatus
description: Martians clear Black Smoke with directed superheated steam; its force shatters windows and burns the curate’s hand.
game_adaptation: A visibly committed sweep or environmental reset in game proposals.

title: Rear metallic carrier / cage
description: A basket-like metal carrier projects behind the fighting-machine and holds captured people.
game_adaptation: A capture objective silhouette or aftermath prop kept at the edge of the battle space.

title: Five-legged handling-machine
description: A spider/crab-like machine has five agile jointed legs, many articulated levers and grasping tentacles, and a controlling Martian visible through a plate. It unpacks, builds and probes hiding places.
game_adaptation: The level-three boss uses a local probing arm, a locked sweep and a lowered coupler reached by ordinary attacks.

title: Digging / excavating machine
description: A smaller mechanism excavates and embanks the pit with rhythmic shocks, green vapour, pipes and whistles; the narrator sees no directing Martian.
game_adaptation: An industrial background mechanism or short ground-warning pattern.

title: Aluminium-making apparatus
description: A milk-can-like body and oscillating pear-shaped receptacle process clay into powder, clinkers and shining aluminium bars, served by a handling-machine.
game_adaptation: A distinctive pit-side industrial prop and source of cool highlights against red-black scenery.
chapter_refs: [{"label": "Book II, Chapter 3: The Days of Imprisonment", "book": "II", "chapter": "3", "title": "The Days of Imprisonment", "note": ""}]
notes: Avoid treating this as a generic human furnace: several unusual receptacles and manipulated flows are described.

title: Artificial muscles and sliding friction joints
description: Martian machinery uses electrically contracting disc-like quasi-muscles in elastic sheaths and curved sliding parts rather than ordinary wheel-dominated mechanisms.
game_adaptation: Close studies of sliding joints, elastic sleeves and telescoping arms distinguish the machine family.
chapter_refs: [{"label": "Book II, Chapter 2: What We Saw from the Ruined House", "book": "II", "chapter": "2", "title": "What We Saw from the Ruined House", "note": ""}]
notes: The mechanism is fictional retrospective explanation; do not claim it as real engineering.

title: Wheel-free Martian machine vocabulary
description: The narrator stresses that the Martians’ devices show no wheel use and little simple fixed-pivot circular motion.
game_adaptation: Keep alien walking/manipulating machines separate from wheeled human transport.
chapter_refs: [{"label": "Book II, Chapter 2: What We Saw from the Ruined House", "book": "II", "chapter": "2", "title": "What We Saw from the Ruined House", "note": ""}]
notes: The cylinder lid rotates, but that does not imply the walking machines should use wheels for locomotion.

title: Flying-machine
description: A flat broad flying form is glimpsed over the coast; the final camp contains a large flying-machine that was being tried in Earth’s denser atmosphere.
game_adaptation: A distant silhouette or dormant final-redoubt prop; optional concept exploration.

title: Blood-injection pipette
description: Martians obtain living blood and inject it through a small pipette into their own vessels instead of eating and digesting.
game_adaptation: A research-sheet detail or implied harvesting station, without an obligatory graphic feeding scene.

title: Martian body and sensory anatomy
description: A roughly four-foot rounded head-body has grey-brown leathery skin, two enormous dark eyes, a fleshy beak-like mouth, one rear ear drum and sixteen slender tentacles in two groups of eight. It lacks nostrils and conventional digestive organs.
game_adaptation: Anatomical character studies, curled pilot silhouette and machine scale reference.

notes: Do not replace this with a two-armed humanoid in armour. The narrator’s early bear-sized impression and later anatomical measurements differ in purpose.

title: Martian physiological limitations and reproduction
description: Earth’s gravity and atmosphere make the unclothed bodies laborious and visibly panting; the narrator reports no sleep and no sex, with reproduction by budding.
game_adaptation: Contrast vulnerable, deliberate flesh with lively machine motion; reserve budding for a research plate.

title: Martian communication hypothesis
description: The narrator interprets silent coordinated work as telepathy and disputes common claims of vocal/gesture communication; elsewhere machine howls accompany signalling or continued machinery.
game_adaptation: Use acoustic motifs and shared machine timing without requiring literal psychic mind-control gameplay.

title: Bipedal provision-creatures from Mars
description: Shrivelled remains suggest fragile six-foot bipeds with silica-like skeletons, weak muscles and large eyes; two or three were brought in cylinders and killed before arrival.
game_adaptation: An appendix specimen study, not a regular living Earth enemy.
chapter_refs: [{"label": "Book II, Chapter 2: What We Saw from the Ruined House", "book": "II", "chapter": "2", "title": "What We Saw from the Ruined House", "note": ""}]
notes: The text presents anatomy from remains and gives no species name, culture or surviving companion character.

title: Red weed
description: A vivid red plant has cactus-like branching and enormous water fronds; it thrives beside streams, chokes rivers and floods meadows, then whitens, shrivels and breaks under disease.
game_adaptation: Core environment family with living crimson, waterlogged red and brittle pale dying states.

title: Red creeper
description: A separate red climbing growth threads up living trees and briefly spreads, but gains less lasting footing than red weed.
game_adaptation: Fine red climbing strands for walls and trunks, separately named in the catalogue.

title: Terrestrial bacteria and disease
description: The narrative explains the Martian and red-weed collapse through terrestrial microbes against which they lack resistance; the epilogue treats the exact explanation as strongly probable rather than fully proved.
game_adaptation: The natural ending: failing machine actions, whitening plants, silent invaders and renewed daylight.

title: Dogs, crows and surviving animals
description: Deer, cows, bats, frogs, cats, rabbits, dogs and birds persist or leave remains in occupied country. Scavenging dogs and crows reveal that Martian power has collapsed.
game_adaptation: Restrained wildlife and silhouettes; crows are a strong ending cue, frogs a tiny persistence-of-life motif.

title: Thunder Child torpedo ram
description: A low heavy ironclad with twin funnels charges the tripods to protect evacuation shipping and destroys two despite being destroyed itself.
game_adaptation: A major human hero machine concept with foam, flame and low iron silhouette.

notes: Thunder Child is a ship, not a named human boss; no film-specific design is canonical to this novel.

title: Human artillery, Maxims and ammunition carts
description: Field guns, concealed batteries, machine guns and giant siege guns are deployed; a well-placed shell destroys a tripod hood and another damages a leg, yet organized defence fails.
game_adaptation: Friendly or abandoned weapon props and broad blast-debris staging.

title: Complacent security before recognition
description: Warm domestic life, music, gardens, Sunday clothes and newspapers continue alongside an approaching catastrophe; people struggle to believe the danger applies to them.
game_adaptation: Begin the act with brief familiar human landmarks already under pressure, trusting the experienced player to read the escalation.

description: Metallic bodies move with astonishing life and precision while human bodies and even Martian flesh remain fragile.
game_adaptation: Mix exquisite moving joints, green industrial vapour and tiny domestic props; show awe and threat together.

description: Crowds, bottlenecks, conflicting reports, thirst and transport failures dissolve ordinary cooperation, though pockets of care persist.

description: Scientific, military, religious and newspaper explanations are repeatedly incomplete or wrong; later accounts retain qualifications.
game_adaptation: Environmental reports and changing interpretations reward the experienced player’s observation of actual tells.

title: Confinement, hunger and moral strain
description: Dark domestic rooms, limited supplies, the probing tentacle and incompatible companions compress dread until survival damages moral judgement.
game_adaptation: Level three becomes a short tense local encounter with rubble, quiet pauses and readable probe commitments.

title: Imperial reversal and animal comparison
description: The opening connects invasion to colonial extermination; human vulnerability and alien feeding expose the way humans dominate other beings.
game_adaptation: Show occupation and human displacement rather than celebrate a simple conquest fantasy.

title: Alien ecological takeover
description: Water channels become red growths and flooded villas, making familiar country resemble another planet.
game_adaptation: Change environmental structure and plant state across the act while keeping floor tells clean and shapes readable.

title: Profound silence after human flight
description: Empty roads, intact closed houses and distant repeated cries feel more disturbing than constant fighting; the cry’s cessation is a shock.
game_adaptation: Use short silent breathing spaces and a local audible/visual cue before final collapse.

title: Hope through ordinary life and natural limits
description: Dogs, birds, frogs, dawn, microbes, kindness and relief reveal that mechanical domination was not absolute.
game_adaptation: Reserve dawn, whitening weed, resting metal and returning human activity for the coda.

title: Trauma and uncertain future after relief
description: Reunion and rebuilding coexist with intrusive memories, insecurity and fear that another attack may come.
game_adaptation: End with a regained path and human contact, while distant metal and an uneasy sky prevent a falsely triumphant total conquest ending.

title: Heat-Ray fighting tripod
description: Canonical basis: a flexible three-legged machine aims a camera-like Heat-Ray, can bend or shorten its legs, and suffers a damaged leg at St. George’s Hill.
game_adaptation: Game proposal: mark the player’s most recent world-space dash endpoint, visibly lock aim, commit the sweep, then lower a leg assembly into ordinary slash range. Bait, evade and punish using existing gestures.

title: Ruined-house handling-machine
description: Canonical basis: a five-legged manipulator unpacks equipment, telescopes its arms and probes through the ruined house into the cellar.
game_adaptation: Game proposal for level three: one visible arm searches a marked lane, locks into a broad sweep, and retracts; attack a reachable lowered manipulator coupler during its recovery to open an escape route.

title: Black Smoke deployment tripod
description: Canonical basis: tripods fire canisters from thick tubes, lay heavy Black Smoke, and clear it with steam.
game_adaptation: Game proposal: canisters visibly choose ground patches with two safe landings; after deployment the unit anchors a lowered tube or support assembly that can be struck at close range. Reuse tripod assets as an alternate challenge.

title: Shepperton river interception
description: Canonical basis: artillery decapitates a tripod at Shepperton; Thunder Child later rams two machines while protecting refugees.
game_adaptation: Game proposal: a riverbank escape set piece uses locked leg placements, steam patches and a lowered damaged leg to clear a civilian route; human support can be shown in the distance.

title: Primrose Hill failing sentry
description: Canonical basis: the narrator approaches motionless tripods and finds the final encampment dead, with bacteria explaining the collapse and birds gathered around the hoods.
game_adaptation: Game proposal for level five: the last still-functioning tripod repeats established locked rays and foot placements, exposes a low brace, and can be disabled enough to escape. The subsequent wider collapse is natural disease, shown by silence, pale weed and birds.

title: Smith’s newspaper concession

game_adaptation: An incidental newspaper-trade annotation rather than a cast portrait.

title: Ray Scout
description: A new game enemy role built from the canonical aimed Heat-Ray and articulated machine vocabulary.
game_adaptation: Proposed A2-E1: a smaller heat-projecting unit visibly locks a short lane after tracking, commits, then exposes a reachable recovery opening. Introduce its changed timing briefly; the player already knows the gestures.

game_adaptation: Proposed A2-E2: announce a local deposit and leave two clean normal-dash landings; a short deployment recovery permits an ordinary close-range attack.

title: Salvage Handler
description: A smaller new gameplay role derived from the novel’s construction and probing handling-machine.
game_adaptation: Proposed A2-E3: a visible telescoping arm marks a short sweep or probe, fixes its lane, and retracts with a reachable recovery opening. Later combinations test landing choices rather than new inputs.
